input.question: Why aren't high rise office fires more common/unsurvivable?
input.ground_truth: They used to, then builders got wise to it. Now we build high rises out of concrete and glass, which don't catch on fire. We restrict how much flammable material is used on the floors of high rises and don't allow anything flammable at all in the stairwells (that's why the stairs are pretty much always barren concrete with metal railings), which makes it more difficult for the fires to spread between floors.

response.prediction: High-rise office fires are not as common or as deadly as people might fear because modern buildings are designed with safety in mind. Buildings have fire-resistant materials, multiple fire alarms, smoke detectors, and sprinkler systems that help detect and control fires quickly. Emergency exits, clearly marked stairwells, and fire doors help people escape safely. Fire departments also respond quickly to alarms and are trained to handle fires in tall buildings. Because of these safety measures, most high-rise office fires are contained or controlled before they become large or deadly.
